text:
alex_k: FYI customer 'AcmeCorp' on Dedicated reported streaming SSE disconnects when routing through their corporate proxy. Direct traffic to the VPC works fine. Symptoms: partial event payload, client reconnect loop, sometimes duplicated fragments. Seen across multiple app instances.

maria_ops: Can you paste the raw client logs and a curl repro? Also which model/route? :eyes:

alex_k: Route: /v1/streams/generate (hosted on dedicated pool). Client logs show connection closed after ~18-22s, server keeps generating. Example client error: `ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR` then reconnect. Customer's infra team says they do TLS-inspection (MITM) and set proxy to chunk-buffering.

sam_support: Repro curl I used from a linux box behind a test corp-proxy (we mirrored their config):

```
curl -v --http1.1 \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --no-buffer \
  "https://dedicated.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-1" 
```

Output shows SSE beginning then abruptly cuts mid-event, then connection FIN. If I hit the same endpoint from a machine with direct internet, stream stays alive and completes.

jon_eng: We captured a tcpdump on the ingress (customer side) and see lots of retransmits and an MSS mismatch. Their proxy rewrites TLS, causing MTU changes and extra headers. Snippet from tcpdump (summary):

```
12:01:22.123 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > 52.40.10.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:14321, ack 1, win 64240
12:01:22.124 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > 52.40.10.11.443: Flags [.], ack 1, win 64240
12:01:22.140 IP 52.40.10.11.443 > 10.0.0.5.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 14321
12:01:22.150 IP 52.40.10.11.443 > 10.0.0.5.52344: Flags [P.], seq 513:1024, ack 14321
12:01:22.160 IP 52.40.10.11.443 > 10.0.0.5.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1025:1536, ack 14321
... then a bunch of [tcp retransmission]
```

egress-bot: Observed 7 retransmits on that connection, average segment size 1408 bytes (prob MTU/headers).

maria_ops: Could the proxy be buffering and re-chunking SSE events into larger TLS records which then get dropped mid-stream? Lots of proxies will reassemble and add headers for inspection, and if they buffer until N bytes, you'll see partial SSE frames delivered then connection resets when internal buffer times out.

alex_k: The partial payloads we saw are mid-JSON; example SSE event we received: `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"…continue here"}}` and then connection closed. Client later reconnects and requests resume but we don't issue a resume token. So app-level dedupe/restart spams tokens/billing.

sam_support: Repro steps for customer engineering:
1) From a host behind their proxy, run the curl above with `--no-buffer` and `--http1.1`.
2) At same time, tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w sse-proxy.pcap host 52.40.10.11 and port 443`
3) Observe `PSH` segments followed by retransmits and a FIN after ~20s.

jon_eng: Quick mitigation suggestions for them:
- Ask proxy admins to disable response buffering / streaming aggregation for the destination host or path (turn off response body buffering / chunk coalescing)
- Add SSE comment heartbeats `:hb\n\n` every 10s to keep proxies from timing out (temporary)
- If they cannot change proxy, route requests through a proxy-bypass egress that preserves TLS (no inspection) for that app.

maria_ops: From our side we can add these server-side workarounds:
- Emit a small initial comment and frequent 8-16 byte keepalive comments so proxies see continuous small writes
- Add `Connection: keep-alive` and an `X-Proxy-No-Buffer: 1` advisory header (best-effort, many proxies ignore but some honor)

jon_eng: Longer-term: runtime should tolerate fragmented TCP delivery and avoid closing SSE on a single mid-frame read error. We should attempt to hold generation until TLS session indicates RST from proxy; but that's tricky. Engineering follow-up to add better reassembly and a resume token for streaming sessions so clients can resume from last committed token.

alex_k: Customer also reported billing spike due to repeated reconnects. We should flag billing for investigaton to avoid charging for duplicated partial outputs while we work with customer.

sam_support: I've opened a support ticket with AcmeCorp with timestamped traces and a short reproducible test. Ticket: SUP-4921. Included pcap and curl logs.

maria_ops: @jon_eng can you pick this up? Also tagging runtime owners. Action items:
- jon_eng: investigate frag-tolerant SSE and resume token design (P0 for dedicated/private correlated issues)
- maria_ops: coordinate with customer on proxy config changes and provide heartbeat snippet
- sam_support: attach the pcap and sample curl to the ticket + advise billing hold

jon_eng: Will take it. Initial plan: create a small patch to emit periodic 12-byte comments and log per-connection retransmit counts. If retransmits > 3 within 30s, flip to degraded mode and emit smaller chunks. Also schedule design doc for resume tokens.

alex_k: Customer confirmed they'll try disabling body-buffering on their proxy and test this afternoon. Will update thread. :thumbsup:

sam_support: Noting workaround for support playbook: add guide "SSE issues with TLS-inspecting proxies" to support docs with tcpdump signs, curl repro, and proxy config snippets.

maria_ops: Thanks team. Keeping ticket SUP-4921 open until fix or customer bypass confirmed.

alex_k: Update 15:40 UTC — AcmeCorp reverted buffering and the stream completed end-to-end. They reported no more partial payloads. Closing loop once customer confirms for 24h. :white_check_mark:
